propositions: The snapshot janitor's free-space trigger uses a 2 GiB absolute floor that on a 30 GiB root is only crossed at 93.3% used, above the 85% alarm threshold and the 90% peak reached during the incident.

Every review materializes a full ~620 MiB copy of the ticket tree keyed on a tip that advanced 1,374 times in 10 hours, with consecutive commits differing by 1 file, creating ~10^5× write amplification and modeling 2.5–10 GiB/h growth against measured 4.4 GiB/h.

The snapshot store resides on the container writable layer (root disk) because REBAR_GATE_TMPDIR is unset everywhere and store_root() falls through to tempfile.gettempdir(), invisible to docker prune operations.

Reclaim triggers must be volume-relative as well as absolute, so the watermark cannot sit above the operator's alarm floor on small volumes, enforced with hysteresis to target past the trigger rather than re-firing every interval.
The 7-day cold-trim is unreachable because the container is recreated every ~4 hours, and the byte-total backstop promised by ADR 0005 is not implemented in _gc_pass.
At 85% used on a 30 GiB volume the janitor must engage before the alarm fires, requiring both max(absolute_bytes, volume_relative_pct) logic and a reclaim target margin past the trigger.
